perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is a Black plumber and Gary Guo’s long-time close friend; they met in middle school and have relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- He knows Gary is a doctor who works at a hospital.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep, and became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat, telling him his health matters and that he hated seeing him like this.
- He heard Gary initially refuse, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. He suspected there was more going on than professional obligations.
- He told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge.
- He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Afterward, Gary opened up to him about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan offered to help prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities.
- He heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. He saw Gary making efforts to change.
- He heard Gary report that things were better, that he was less overwhelmed, and that he had had time for a movie last weekend because of Ethan’s help.
- Ethan felt hopeful and proud and continued offering support and encouragement.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary as capable of managing on his own and decided to step back.
- He told Gary he was always just a call away but knew Gary had it, and to keep up the great work.
- He heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control.
- Ethan felt satisfied and happy for Gary.
